newsitem.title: UK: British Land shares firm on annual results.
newsitem.headline: British Land shares firm on annual results.

text.p: Shares in British Land Plc firmed on Wednesday after the property company reported annual pre-tax profits ahead of expectations and a net asset value (NAV) which was broadly in line with forecasts.
Analysts said the results were encouraging but some warned that there was unlikely to be much more upside for the share price.
"The profit figures were excellent," said Nan Rogers, analyst at Charterhouse Tilney. "We will be increasing our profit forecast for next year."
The shares were 3-1/2p higher at 591 by 0846 GMT.
British Land reported pre-tax profits of 91.2 million stg in the year to end-March, compared with a forecast range of 75 to 79 million. The NAV was 487p, within the forecast range of 471 to 503.

Rogers said she was forecasting a NAV of around 570p for the current financial year, but pointed out that this was less than the share price. She said she expected the shares to drift off over the summer.
"It's a great company, wonderful numbers but it's all in the share price already," she said.
She said she was slightly disappointed with the performance of the company's assets, such as supermarkets.
Another analyst, who asked not be be named, said the headline profit figure was excellent and the underlying picture was "relatively positive".
"They are a very solid set of results," he said.
